paragraphs: I am a middle school student, and I have a simple daily routine that keeps me fit. I get up at six thirty and run for twenty minutes in the park nearby. After that, I eat a healthy breakfast with milk, eggs and fruit at the table.

At school, I listen to the teacher carefully and do my homework on time each day. In the evening, I help my mother with the housework and then look at books. On weekends, I play basketball with my friends for an hour on the court.

Eighty percent of my classmates say they exercise. We all know good habits give us energy and keep our bodies strong and active. My lifestyle is not special, but it makes me happy and ready for each new day ahead.

paragraphs: Good habits are like seeds. If you plant them early, they grow into a healthy life. Exercise is one of the most important habits. It makes your body strong and your mind clear. A good breakfast gives you energy. Students who eat well get better results at school.

Enough sleep is another key habit. Children need about nine hours of sleep each night. Reading every day also helps. It builds your vocabulary and opens your mind to new ideas. Less sugar and fewer snacks keep your teeth and your weight in good shape for years.

Scientists say people with healthy habits live longer and feel happier than others do. Small daily actions, done again and again, become strong and useful habits over time. The earlier you start, the easier it is to keep a healthy lifestyle for the rest of life.

questions.q: What does the writer compare good habits to?
How much sleep do children need each night?
What does reading every day help build?
According to scientists, what do healthy habits bring?

paragraphs: Do you want to build a good habit? Here are some steps that really work for students. First, choose only one small habit. Do not try to change everything in a single day. Set a clear goal. For example, walk for fifteen minutes after dinner three times a week.

Place a note on your desk so you remember to do it every morning when you wake up. Find a friend to join you. When you exercise together, it is easier to keep going. Keep a small diary of your progress. Seeing your success makes you want to continue.

Do not give up if you miss one day. Start again the next morning and keep moving on. Good habits take time, but if you repeat the action daily, it becomes a natural part of you. Ask a friend to join you so you can help each other stay on track.

paragraphs: Ann is a healthy girl. Every morning she jogs for fifteen minutes in the park near her home. She eats a good breakfast with milk and fruit, and she never eats too much sugar. After school she does her homework on time and then looks at books for half an hour.

On weekends she plays basketball with friends. She says sports give her energy to learn. Her brother also jogs with her, and their mother is happy to see the children so active. They believe a healthy lifestyle is the best gift a family can give to growing children.
